ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows one large rectangular garden. It is split into a left vertical rectangle labeled Flowers and a right column. The right column is divided horizontally into an upper rectangle labeled Vegetables and a lower rectangle labeled Strawberries. The top label 2 m spans the width of the Flowers rectangle. The right-side vertical label 3 m spans the height of the Strawberries rectangle. Reasoning: The Flowers rectangle has area 10 m² and width 2 m, so the full height of the garden is 10 ÷ 2 = 5 m. The whole garden has area 30 m², so its total width is 30 ÷ 5 = 6 m. Since the Flowers part is 2 m wide, the right column is 6 − 2 = 4 m wide. The Strawberries part has height 3 m, so the Vegetables part has height 5 − 3 = 2 m. Therefore, the Vegetables area is 4 × 2 = 8 m².
